question: As a ward nurse handling hospital tools every day, what is your main responsibility regarding them?

options.A: Acting as primary custodian and daily operator
options.C: Designing and manufacturing new medical devices
options.D: Repairing all electrical faults on the ward

explanation: You use these tools right at the bedside every day, which means you are the key person making sure they are handled and checked properly!

question: Why is taking good care of ward equipment so important for your patients?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to pay for broken items
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for hospital biomedical engineers
options.C: It ensures devices provide reliable therapy and diagnostics
options.D: It stops patients from asking questions about machinery

explanation: When equipment is well-maintained, it works accurately and keeps our patients safe from harm or wrong results. Great job keeping your patients safe!

question: Which of these devices is a great example of therapeutic equipment used to treat a patient?
explanation: Therapeutic equipment actively helps treat conditions and aids recovery. A nebulizer does this brilliantly by delivering medication straight to the airways!

question: Why must disposable medical supplies never be reused for another patient?

options.C: Because the plastic degrades if washed once
options.D: To make more room in hospital supply rooms

explanation: Single-use items are made for one time only. Tossing them out after use stops infections from spreading between patients.

question: What is the safest way to unplug a machine from the wall socket on the ward?

options.A: Grip the molded plug firmly and pull straight out
options.B: Pull the device across the room until it unplugs
options.C: Yank the flexible cord until the plug pops loose
options.D: Switch off the main circuit breaker for the ward

explanation: Always hold the solid plug itself! Pulling by the cord damages the internal wires and can cause a nasty spark.

question: You spot an infusion pump cord stretched tightly across a busy hospital walkway. What should you do right away?

options.A: Cover the cord with a wet towel to make it more visible
options.B: Leave it alone because pumps need power to stay functional
options.C: Unplug the pump and run it entirely on low battery power
options.D: Reroute the cord safely out of the walkway to prevent tripping

explanation: Cords across walkways are dangerous tripping hazards for staff and visitors. Moving it safely out of the way keeps everyone walking safely!

question: Why must you always physically wash and clean an instrument before disinfecting or sterilizing it?

options.A: Soap adds an extra layer of electrical insulation
options.B: Disinfectants will melt dirty plastic surfaces
options.C: Organic matter protects germs from chemical agents
options.D: It makes the equipment look shiny for visitors

explanation: Dirt, blood, or body fluids act like a shield for germs. Cleaning washes that shield away so the disinfectant can actually reach and kill the bugs!

question: Which process is needed to completely destroy tough bacterial spores on surgical instruments?
explanation: Only full sterilization methods (like using an autoclave) are powerful enough to wipe out all germs and stubborn bacterial spores.

question: What is the main reason we do routine inventory checks for ward equipment?

options.A: Tracking missing items and keeping emergency tools ready
options.B: Finding out which nurse uses the most supplies
options.C: Permanently locking away expensive diagnostic machines
options.D: Increasing the financial taxes paid by the hospital

explanation: Inventory checks make sure everything we need is present and accounted for before an emergency hits the ward.

question: How should you store battery-operated mobile equipment when you are not using it?

options.A: Unplugged and drained completely to save electricity
options.B: Stored outdoors to ensure adequate ventilation
options.C: Kept in a dark closet with the battery fully removed
options.D: Plugged into a power source to maintain battery charge

explanation: Leaving it plugged in keeps the battery full and ready to go for the next clinical emergency!

question: What is the FIRST thing you should do if a piece of equipment acts up while you are caring for a patient?

options.A: Remove the faulty item and replace it with a working one
options.B: Leave it plugged in so the next shift can look at it
options.C: Try to fix the internal wiring with electrical tape
options.D: Write an incident report for the hospital director

explanation: Patient safety comes first! Always take away the broken device and grab a working replacement right away.

question: Why is it unsafe to use ordinary adhesive tape to fix a frayed electrical cord on a medical device?

options.A: Adhesive residue ruins the texture of the plastic casing
options.B: Tape does not provide safe insulation against electrical shock
options.C: It prevents the biomedical engineers from seeing the color
options.D: It makes the equipment look untidy during hospital rounds

explanation: Quick tape fixes don't have the proper safety protection to stop electrical shocks or short circuits. Always tag it for biomedical engineering instead!
